## LanDrop v0.3.0

This release is about uploads: what happens when one is interrupted, cancelled,
or silently corrupted. Downloads and the sharing model are unchanged — point
LanDrop at a folder, start the service, open the address on another device.

### Highlights

- **A partial file can no longer look complete.** Bytes land in a `.part` file
  and are renamed onto the real name only when the written total matches the
  declared size. An interrupted upload stays invisible in the listing instead of
  appearing as a file somebody can open.
- **Resume that survives a real interruption.** Uploads run in 32 MB chunks. A
  dropped link resumes from the server's byte count, guarded by a size and
  modification-time fingerprint so two files sharing a name are never spliced
  together.
- **Per-chunk checksums.** Every chunk carries a CRC32; the server hashes while
  writing, rolls the staging file back to the chunk boundary on a mismatch, and
  the browser resends that chunk. A 16-bit TCP checksum, usually computed by the
  network card, misses more than people assume.
- **Cancelling means cancelling.** A cancel button stops the whole queue
  immediately. Cancelling and stopping the service discard the staged data; only
  an unexpected failure keeps it, for a resume.
- **Both ends agree on what happened.** The desktop list distinguishes running,
  done, failed and cancelled instead of reporting every interruption as a
  network fault, and the browser page notices within seconds when the service
  has been stopped.
- **Folder upload and drag-and-drop.** Drop files or folders onto the page, or
  pick a folder. Relative paths are preserved and empty directories are created.
- **Hide actually hides.** The upload panel no longer reopens itself on every
  progress update; a floating pill brings it back when you want it.
- **`zh-Hans` instead of `zh-CN`.** The language tag now names the script rather
  than a region. Existing configuration files keep working.

### Downloads

| Platform | File | Install |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | `LanDrop-windows-amd64.exe` | Portable — just run it |
| Linux | `LanDrop-linux-amd64.deb` | `sudo apt install ./LanDrop-linux-amd64.deb` |

On first launch, allow the firewall / local network prompt — otherwise other
devices cannot connect.

### Notes

- Files uploaded by earlier versions are untouched; staging only applies to new
  transfers.
- A `.part` file nobody came back for is reclaimed after seven days.
- The browser page reloads itself when the server it is talking to has been
  rebuilt, which used to look like a change that never took effect.
